question.leadin: Answer the following about weird Chinese emperors.
question.text: This dynasty's emperor Toghon Temur once considered the idea of killing everyone with the surnames Zhang, Wang, Liu, Li, and Zhao, which would've killed more than 90% of China's population. This dynasty was established in China by Kublai Khan.
question.clue: One man who accompanied this dynasty's princess Kokochin to Persia served as a tax collector here and wrote extensively of this dynasty's salt trade.

swap.leadin: In his pseudo-historical book 1421, Gavin Menzies claimed that an explorer from this dynasty visited the Americas before Christopher Columbus.
swap.text: Name this Chinese dynasty, renowned for its blue and white porcelain, which succeeded the Yuan dynasty and preceded the Qing dynasty.
swap.clue: During this dynasty, the Yongle Emperor began construction of the Forbidden City and ordered several naval expeditions led by Zheng He.

question.leadin: The failed Hundred Days' Reform occurred during this event.
question.text: Name this uprising against foreigners by the Society of Righteous and Harmonious Fists which saw the Empress Dowager Cixi declare war on an eight nation alliance.
question.clue: The International Legations were besieged during this conflict that arose out of resentment over unequal treaties such as those of Wangxia and Nanking.

swap.text: The construction of over six thousand backyard steel furnaces was a part of this economic policy by which Mao planned for China to modernize in a short period of time.
swap.answerHtml: Great Leap Forward [also accept Second Five-Year Plan or Dayuejin]
swap.clue: Millions of people were encouraged to set up backyard furnaces during this campaign.

question.text: The treaty ending the First Opium War was signed in this city. It was later the capital of the Kuomintang regime before and after the Second Sino-Japanese War.
question.clue: A contest to kill one hundred people with a sword took place in this city, which was once the site of the Porcelain Tower.

swap.text: Pu Yi was forced to abdicate by this man, who later set up a provisional government as the second president of the Republic of China after Sun Yat-sen. In 1915, he briefly ruled as the Hongxian Emperor.
swap.clue: Supposedly nursing a foot ailment with the Qing Dynasty fell, he was later thought to be behind the assassination of Song Jiaoren.

question.text: Chiang succeeded Sun Yat-Sen as leader of this Chinese political party, which has governed Taiwan for 80 years.
question.clue: This faction opened the Whampoa Academy during the 1920s, in which it began several campaigns to end the Warlord Era.

swap.text: Ma Ying-jeou overwhelmingly defeated Frank Hsieh, winning all of the 24 districts except for the counties of Yunlin, Chiayi, Tainan, Kaohsiung, and Pingtung in this country.
swap.answerHtml: Republic of China (accept Taiwan, do not accept or prompt just “China” or “People’s Republic of China”)
swap.clue: This government reunified its country by defeating a rival government in the Northern Expedition.

question.leadin: Identify these figures from a certain country in the 20th century.
question.text: Forced to work in a tractor factory after he was purged, this man was rehabilitated and became party chairman in 1981, overseeing China's economic opening.
question.clue: This successor of Hua Guofeng introduced free enterprise to his country with the"socialism with Chinese characteristics" policy.

swap.text: Stories of Bo's ruthlessness include one where he beat up his father while a member of one of these groups known as United Action. Mao encouraged the formation of these student-led paramilitary groups during the Cultural Revolution.
swap.clue: The leaders of the Eleventh Plenary Session ratified the Sixteen Articles and instructed this group to fight the "Four Olds."

question.text: The Kingdom of Kong, which is sometimes classed as one of the jihad states, was founded by the Dyula people, a caste of this profession. In medieval Eurasia, people of this occupation travelled with their goods on the Silk Road.
question.clue: Under the cohong system, members of this occupation operated out of the Thirteen Factories at Canton.

swap.leadin: In 69 AD, Rome was ruled by this number of emperors in succession.
swap.text: Name this number of co-emperors who ruled in the Diocletian-established Tetrarchy.
swap.clue: The Algerian War of Independence led to the collapse of the French republic of this number. The Knights Templar were disbanded under a French king of this regnal number nicknamed "The Fair."

question.leadin: He shares his name with the Tang emperor who was the husband of Empress Wu and conquered Korea in 668.
question.text: Name this emperor who ruled from 1127 to 1187, using his general Yue Fei to hold off the invasions of the Juchen and fortify the southern part of the former empire.

swap.text: The Baltic countries gained independence from the Soviet Union in a "revolution" named for this action. That revolution named for this action included the formation of a human chain across all three countries.
swap.answerHtml: singing [accept Singing Revolution or laulev revolutsioon or dziesmotā revolūcija or dainuojanti revoliucija]
swap.clue: The Tibeto-Burman Lisu people pass on their history through works in this art form which may take a whole night to perform. The all-women group Tyva Kyzy popularized a variety of this musical performance called Khoomei native to and often named for the country of Tuva.

question.leadin: Answer the following about the history of standardized testing in China.
question.text: Original-language term required. This highest degree of the imperial examination was extremely difficult, but passing it made one a member of China's bureaucratic elite. The emperor himself sometimes proctored this degree's exam.
question.answerHtml: jinshi (“JEEN-shurr”) [or jìnshì; prompt on Imperial Scholars; prompt on Metropolitan Exam by asking “what degree did that confer?”]
question.clue: After passing the final Metropolitan Exam, candidates were awarded this highest and final degree. The purchasing of this degree toward the end of the Qing (ching) meant the "Imperial Scholars" who held it were no longer guaranteed the highest offices.

swap.leadin: This dynasty's founder, Wendi, built a city with two walled markets, an Eastern Market for domestic goods and a Western Market for foreign goods, which served as the eastern terminus of the Silk Road.
swap.text: Name this dynasty, which built its capital Daxing on the site of Chang'an. This Dynasty began construction on the Grand Canal.
swap.clue: This dynasty managed to defeat the formidable war elephants of the Champa in Vietnam, and possibly one of the greatest architectural advancements during this dynasty was Emperor Wen's construction of the Grand Canal.

question.leadin: Answer the following about the Zhou dynasty.
question.text: You can read about the Spring and Autumn period of the Zhou dynasty in this man's The Spring and Autumn Annals. This historian also authored Shiji and Records of the Grand Historian.
question.clue: This court eunuch wrote a biography of emperors starting with Huangdi, also known as the Yellow Emperor, to his contemporary Emperor Wu of Han.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about a Chinese province.
swap.text: The Xiang River runs through this Chinese province whose name means "south of the lake" due to its proximity to Lake Dongting. Mao Zedong established a short-lived namesake soviet here in 1927 after the Autumn Harvest Uprising.

question.leadin: Answer the following about the state of Wei after Cao Cao's death.
question.text: Members of this clan served as regents of the Wei state starting with Yi. Another member of this clan named Qian, wrote the Records of the Grand Historian.
question.clue: The Three Rebellions in Shouchun began after one member of this clan usurped the regency for Cao Shuang from the Cao clan during the Incident at the Gaoping Tombs.

swap.leadin: Answer some questions about Gwanggaeto's northern conquests.
swap.text: Gwanggaeto destroyed three tribes of the Baili clan, who were members of this ethnic group ruled by the Liao dynasty. These Proto-Mongols had earlier split off from the Kumo Xi.
swap.clue: They divided their holdings into the Northern and Southern Chancellories and their emperors included men such as Shengzong and Jingzong, while their first ruler took the name Taizu and was known as Abaoji.
